items.text: Raymond James contrasts its 'powerfully personal' value proposition with 'other firms' that talk about IRRs and exit periods in three to five years; RJF focuses instead on personal relationships with financial advisors and their clients.
items.quote: other firms are talking about IRRs and exit periods in three to five years, or funnels and all sorts of impersonal things. What we're doing in that world... is really doubling and tripling down on what we've always done, which is really focusing on the personal relationships with financial advisors

items.text: Shoukry says Raymond James does not lead with the highest check but leads with culture and capabilities, which it calls a true differentiated value proposition.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check... we lead with culture and capabilities. And so we have a true differentiated value proposition.

items.text: Shoukry says many competitors that also focus on personal relationships and have similar cultures invest a fraction of Raymond James's technology spend, while RJF's long-term focus and personal relationships differentiate it.
items.quote: a lot of our competitors who also are focused on personal relationships, and that have similar cultures, their technology investment, for example, is a fraction of ours.

items.text: Raymond James says its AI/technology investments are ones smaller regional firms and many independent firms can't afford, and PE-backed firms won't make because of multi-year payback periods and short exit horizons.
items.quote: These are investments that the smaller regional firms and a lot of the independent firms can't afford to make. Some of the PE-backed firms aren't willing to make that long-term investment because these are payback periods of multiple years.

items.text: In Canada, RJF says its 'best of both worlds' value proposition is similar to the U.S.: a more advisor-centric culture plus all the capabilities advisors coming from the big six banks are used to.
items.quote: We offer a more advisor-centric culture and all the capabilities that the advisors, that most of them come from those banks have become accustomed to having.

items.text: RJF describes its differentiated value proposition as advisers not having to choose between culture and capabilities—an adviser- and client-focused culture plus leading technology, products and solutions.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: RJF says its client-first culture, robust technology and product platforms and strong balance sheet continue to differentiate it as a destination of choice for advisers.
items.quote: Our client-first culture, together with our robust technology and product platforms and strong balance sheet, continues to differentiate Raymond James as a destination of choice for financial advisers across our affiliation options.

items.text: RJF says having the culture, products, platform and technology is differentiating it more than ever.
items.quote: having the culture and the products and the platform and the technology is really differentiating us more than ever.

cells.reason: The passages contain Raymond James's own contrastive statements about how its value proposition differs from competitors, which is the RJF-side evidence for the comparison.
